calls.head: Something has to give
calls.body: The Oilers are the league’s best for the power play, but the Hurricanes are one of the best at the penalty kill. Our lean: the Oilers’ power play wins out. Power plays usually beat kills in these spots. Edmonton has had one of the league’s most effective power plays, and Carolina has had one of the league’s best penalty kills for years.
calls.call: The Oilers’ power play creates more than the league-average 7.6 expected goals per 60 against the Hurricanes.

calls.head: The Oilers like Formenton’s line against Nadeau’s
calls.body: At home, the Oilers keep sending Formenton’s line (Formenton, Michaels and Joseph) out against opponents’ third lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Mike Babcock keeps choosing line for line. Tonight the Hurricanes’ third line is Nadeau, Kotkaniemi and Deslauriers.
calls.call: The Oilers’ L3 (Formenton, Michaels and Joseph) spends at least 34% of its 5-on-5 time against the Hurricanes’ third line.

calls.head: The Hurricanes roll four lines, the Oilers lean on their top six
calls.body: On depth, Carolina is one of the league’s best, but Edmonton is the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. If this one comes down to the bottom six, that suits the Hurricanes.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Ehlers reaches 600 points, but the Hurricanes lose
paras: Talk about a finish. Ryan Nugent-Hopkins played his first game of the season, after missing the first nine. Leon Draisaitl opened the scoring for the Oilers on the power play midway through the first. Jackson Blake made it 1-1 for Carolina on the power play less than three minutes later. The second period was a wild one. Sebastian Aho gave the Hurricanes the lead just 30 seconds into the period, but Nugent-Hopkins tied it up for Edmonton on the power play just under four minutes later. Jarvis put the Hurricanes ahead 3-2 midway through the period. Logan Stankoven made it 4-2 just under five minutes later, with Nikolaj Ehlers picking up his 600th NHL point on the assist. The third period was a wild one. The Oilers’ Mattias Ekholm left early in the period and didn’t return. Connor McDavid cut Carolina’s lead to 4-3 just 26 seconds into the period. Draisaitl struck again on the power play two and a half minutes later to tie it 4-4, his fifth straight game with a goal. Juuso Välimäki scored his first goal for Carolina with less than three minutes left to put the Hurricanes ahead 5-4. McDavid scored again with a minute and a half left to tie it 5-5. Nugent-Hopkins scored the only goal of the shootout for the Oilers. Draisaitl added three assists for a five-point night, and McDavid had three assists for a five-point night.
The chances were close to even, so this one could have gone either way. Devon Levi made 22 saves for the Oilers, and Brandon Bussi allowed five goals on 21 shots.
The Oilers went 3-for-5 on the power play. The Hurricanes hit a post and the crossbar and came up a goal short. The Oil moved to 8-1-1, and the Hurricanes dropped to 8-2-2.
